<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">PART I</font></b><a name="PartI_111214"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Forward-Looking Statements</font></u></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">This Form 10-K contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.&#160; Our actual results could differ materially from those set forth in each forward-looking statement.&#160; Certain factors that might cause such a difference are discussed in this report, including in the section entitled &#147;Forward-Looking Statements&#148; on page 59 of this Form 10-K.</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 1.</font></u></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160; <u>Business</u></font></b><a name="Item1_Business_111209"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Home Properties, Inc. (&#147;Home Properties&#148; or the &#147;Company&#148;) was formed in November 1993 as a Maryland corporation.&#160; Home Properties is a self-administered and self-managed real estate investment trust (&#147;REIT&#148;) that owns, operates, acquires and repositions apartment communities in suburbs of major metropolitan areas, primarily along the East Coast of the United States.&#160; The Company completed an initial public offering of 5,408,000 shares of common stock (the &#147;IPO&#148;) on August 4, 1994 and is traded on the New York Stock Exchange (&#147;NYSE&#148;) under the symbol &#147;HME&#148;.&#160; The Company is included in S&amp;P&#146;s MidCap 400 Index.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company conducts its business through Home Properties, L.P. (the &#147;Operating Partnership&#148;), a New York limited partnership, and a management company, Home Properties Resident Services, Inc. (&#147;HPRS&#148;), a Maryland corporation.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company held 85.2% (84.8% at December&nbsp;31, 2013) of the limited partnership units in the Operating Partnership (&#147;UPREIT Units&#148;).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Home Properties, through its affiliates described above, owned and operated 121 communities with 42,107 apartment units (the &#147;Communities&#148; or the &#147;Properties&#148;) as of December 31, 2014:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="right" style="margin:1.0pt 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s mission is to maximize long-term shareholder value by acquiring, repositioning, managing and owning market-rate apartment communities while enhancing the quality of life for our residents and providing employees with opportunities for growth and accomplishment.&#160; Our vision is to be a prominent owner and manager of market-rate apartment communities located in high barrier, high growth markets.&#160; We expect to maintain or grow portfolios in markets that profitably support our mission as economic conditions&nbsp;permit.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company (continued)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s long-term business strategies include:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">proactively managing and improving our communities to increase net operating income;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">acquiring additional apartment communities with attractive returns at prices that provide a positive spread over the Company&#146;s long-term cost of capital;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">disposing of properties that have reached their potential, are less efficient to operate, or are located in markets where growth has slowed to a pace below that of the markets targeted for acquisition; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">maintaining a strong and flexible capital structure with cost-effective access to the capital markets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Structure</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company was formed in November 1993 as a Maryland corporation and is the general partner of the Operating Partnership.&#160; On December&nbsp;31, 2014, it held an 85.2% partnership interest in the Operating Partnership comprised of: a 1.0% interest as sole general partner; and an 84.2% limited partner interest through its wholly owned subsidiary, Home Properties I, LLC, which owns 100% of Home Properties Trust, the actual limited partner of the Operating Partnership.&#160; The holders of the remaining 14.8% of the UPREIT Units are certain individuals and entities who received UPREIT Units as consideration for their interests in entities owning apartment communities purchased by the Operating Partnership, including certain officers of the Company.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Operating Partnership is a New York limited partnership formed in December&nbsp;1993.&#160; Holders of UPREIT Units in the Operating Partnership may redeem an UPREIT Unit for one share of the Company&#146;s common stock or cash equal to the fair market value at the time of the redemption, at the option of the Company.&#160; Management expects that it will continue to utilize UPREIT Units as a form of consideration for a portion of its acquisition properties when it is economical to do so.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">HPRS is wholly owned by the&nbsp;Operating Partnership, and as a result, the accompanying consolidated financial statements include the accounts of both companies.&#160; HPRS is a taxable REIT subsidiary under the Tax Relief Extension Act of 1999.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September 1997, Home Properties Trust (&#147;the QRS&#148;) was formed as a Maryland real estate trust and as a qualified REIT subsidiary.&#160; The QRS is wholly owned by Home Properties I, LLC which is owned 100% by the Company.&#160; The QRS is a limited partner of the Operating Partnership and holds all of the Company&#146;s interest in the Operating&nbsp;Partnership, except for the 1% held directly by the Company as sole general partner.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company currently has approximately 1,200 employees and its executive offices are located at 850&nbsp;Clinton Square, Rochester, New York 14604.&#160; Its telephone number is (585) 546-4900.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operating Strategies</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company will continue to focus on enhancing long-term investment returns by:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">acquiring apartment communities and repositioning them for long-term growth at prices that provide a positive spread over the Company&#146;s long-term cost of capital;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">recycling assets by disposing of properties in low-growth markets and those that have reached their potential or are less efficient to operate due to size or remote location;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">balancing a decentralized property management philosophy with the efficiencies of centralized support functions and accountability, including rent optimization and volume purchasing;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">enhancing the quality of living for residents by improving service and physical amenities at each community in an environmentally responsible manner;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">adopting new technology to minimize time and cost of administration and maximize efforts to attract and serve residents;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">utilizing its written &#147;Pledge&#148; of customer satisfaction, the foundation on which the Company&#146;s brand was built; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">focusing on expense control while improving the level of service to residents.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a strategy of acquiring mature C/B- apartment communities and repositioning them to B/B+ properties.&nbsp; Since its 1994 IPO, the Company has acquired and redeveloped 224 communities, containing approximately 63,000 units.&nbsp; The repositioning process targets a minimum 10% cash-on-cash return on investment.&nbsp; It is expected that capital expenditures in 2015 for repositioning activities will be in-line with 2014 levels, as residents continue to prefer an upgraded apartment at a higher monthly rent in a recovering economic environment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of the Company&#146;s long and successful history in the redevelopment of apartment communities, our employees have significant design and construction management skills.&#160; The complete repositioning of a community can take place over a five to seven year period.&nbsp; The comprehensive process typically begins with improvements in landscaping, signage and common areas.&nbsp; Exterior improvements increase curb appeal and marketability of the property.&nbsp; Deferred maintenance is corrected, which can include new HVAC systems, roofs, balconies and windows.&nbsp; At many properties, community centers and swimming pools are added or upgraded.&nbsp; Apartment interiors are renovated when residents move out, with the most significant investments made in the upgrade of kitchens and baths.&nbsp; Complete remodeling of dated kitchens and bathrooms typically includes new appliances, flooring, counters, cabinets, lighting, tile, fixtures, sinks, bathtubs and toilets.&nbsp; It may include the removal of kitchen walls to create an open concept living space.&nbsp; When feasible, in-unit washers and dryers are added.&#160; Repositioning efforts significantly increase a property&#146;s rental income, net operating income and market value.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">5<a name="PB_5_104423_2897"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Acquisition, Disposition and Development Strategies</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s strategy is to grow primarily through acquisitions in the suburbs of major metropolitan markets that are near public transportation and major highways and have significant barriers to new construction, limited new apartment supply, easy access to the Company&#146;s headquarters and sufficient apartments available for acquisition to achieve a critical mass.&#160; Other characteristics of targeted markets include:&#160; acquisition opportunities below replacement costs, a mature housing stock, high average single-family home prices, a favorable supply/demand relationship, stable or moderate job growth, reduced vulnerability to economic downturns and large prime renter populations including immigrants and young adults in their twenties and early thirties.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company currently expects its growth to occur within its eight existing markets.&#160; The Company&#146;s largest markets include the suburbs of Baltimore, Boston, New York City, Philadelphia and Washington, D.C.&#160; Continued geographic specialization is expected to have a greater impact on operating efficiencies as compared to the widespread accumulation of properties.&#160; The Company will continue to pursue the acquisition of individual properties as well as multi-property portfolios.&#160; It may also consider strategic investments in other apartment companies, as well as strategic alliances.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2014, the Company acquired three communities in suburban Philadelphia and Chicago with a total of 1,052 units for an aggregate consideration of $142 million, or an average of approximately $134,500 per apartment unit.&#160; The weighted average expected first year capitalization rate for the acquired communities was 6.3%.&#160; Capitalization rate (&#147;cap rate&#148;) is defined as the rate of interest used to convert the first year expected net operating income (&#147;NOI&#148;) less a 2.7% management fee into a single present value.&#160; NOI is defined by the Company as rental income and property other income less operating and maintenance expenses.&#160; For a reconciliation of NOI to income from continuing operations, please refer to Note 12 to Consolidated Financial Statements, under Part IV, Item 15 of this Form 10-K.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company believes that it will have the opportunity to make acquisitions during 2015 and has projected $250 million to $350&nbsp;million in purchases for the year.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company sold three communities in 2014 with a total of 1,527 units for approximately $217 million, resulting in a weighted average unlevered internal rate of return (&#147;IRR&#148;) of 10.0%.&#160; IRR is defined as the discount rate at which the present value of the future cash flows of the investment is equal to the cost of the investment.&#160; The Company sold four communities in 2013 with a total of 1,013 units for approximately $192 million, resulting in a weighted average IRR of 11.3%.&#160; The Company has identified additional communities for sale in 2015 and will continue to evaluate the sale of its communities.&#160; The Company expects to dispose of between $100 million and $200 million of properties in 2015.&#160; Typically, a property will be targeted for sale if management believes that it has reached its potential or if it is located in a slower growth market or is less efficient to operate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company announced in July 2014 that it was exiting the business of developing new apartment communities. The two projects currently under construction will be completed - Eleven55 Ripley in Silver Spring, Maryland and The Courts at Spring Mill Station in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania. No additional new apartment communities will be started. Land parcels that will not be developed are being marketed for sale.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management believes it is in the best interest of the Company&#146;s stockholders to dissolve the new development platform and focus 100% on the Company&#146;s core differentiating strategy of acquiring and redeveloping mature apartment communities. This change in strategy is a positive one as it simplifies the investment story for the Company, reduces risk, and allows management to spend more time on what the Company does best - own, operate, acquire, and reposition Class C/B apartment communities.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">6<a name="PB_6_104459_3020"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financing and Capital Strategies</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company intends to continue to adhere to the following financing policies:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">maintaining a ratio of debt-to-total value (total debt of the Company as a percentage of the value (using the Company&#146;s value as calculated under the terms of the line of credit facility)) of approximately 38.0% or less;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">utilizing primarily fixed rate debt;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">varying debt maturities to avoid significant exposure to interest rate changes upon refinancing; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">maintaining a line of credit so that it can respond quickly to acquisition opportunities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company&#146;s debt was approximately $2.5 billion and the debt-to-total market capitalization ratio was 35.6% based on the year-end closing price of the Company&#146;s common stock of $65.60.&#160; The weighted average interest rate on the Company&#146;s mortgage debt as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 was 5.17% and the weighted average maturity was approximately three and a half years.&#160; Debt maturities are staggered.&#160; Excluding the Company&#146;s line of credit and 180-day bank term loan balance as of December 31, 2014, an average of 14.3% of loans mature each of the next seven years ranging from a high of 24.3% in 2018 to a low of 8.7% in 2017.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company had a $450 million unsecured line of credit facility with M&amp;T Bank and U.S. Bank National Association (acting as joint lead banks) and nine other participating commercial banks with $269 million outstanding on the line of credit.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company further strengthened its balance sheet and increased its financial flexibility during 2014 as follows:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:12.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company received a published investment grade credit rating of BBB from Standard &amp; Poor&#146;s Ratings Services to complement its existing Baa2 rating from Moody&#146;s Investor Services and BBB rating from Fitch Ratings.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:12.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company increased the value of unencumbered properties in relationship to the total property portfolio from 47.8% to 52.8%.&#160; This higher level adds flexibility, allowing the Company to place additional unsecured financing or increase secured borrowing on unencumbered assets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:12.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Government Sponsored Enterprises (&#147;GSEs&#148;) Fannie&nbsp;Mae and Freddie Mac are still active lending to apartment owners.&#160; However, no secured debt was added during 2014, except for one loan assumed in conjunction with a property acquisition.&#160; The Company paid off approximately $180 million of mortgage debt in 2014 with a weighted average interest rate of 4.30%.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financing and Capital Strategies (continued)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The capital market initiatives described above allowed the Company to achieve stronger key debt and credit metrics at December 31, 2014 versus December 31, 2013 as follows:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">total debt to value was reduced to 38.0% from 38.5%; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">(1)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">total secured debt to value was reduced to 25.3% from 28.4%; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">(1)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">net debt to EBITDA (net income before interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization) was reduced to 6.0 times from 6.1 times;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">interest coverage ratio was increased to 4.0 times from 3.5 times;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">fixed charge coverage ratio increased to 3.7 times from 3.3 times; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the value of the unencumbered asset pool was increased to $3.4 billion from $3.0 billion; or to 52.8% from 47.7% of total value, respectively.</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;"> (1)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">(1)&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Value as calculated under the terms of the line of credit facility.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For 2015, the Company plans to continue to increase the level of the value of unencumbered properties to approximately 58% of the portfolio, maintaining the debt-to-total value ratio at a level equal to or slightly less than the level at December&nbsp;31, 2014 and utilizing more unsecured debt with minimal reliance on new secured debt.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management expects to continue to fund a portion of its continued growth by taking advantage of its UPREIT structure and using UPREIT Units as currency in acquisition transactions.&#160; It is difficult to predict the level of demand from sellers for this type of transaction.&#160; In periods when the Company&#146;s stock price is trading at a discount to estimated net asset value (&#147;NAV&#148;) per share, it is unlikely that management would engage in UPREIT transactions.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s strategy is to opportunistically repurchase shares at a discount to its estimated NAV, thereby continuing to build value for long-term shareholders.&#160; The last year where the Company repurchased any shares under this program was 2008.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014, there was approval remaining to purchase 2.3 million shares.&#160; Management does not anticipate making share repurchases in 2015.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Competition</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s properties are primarily located in developed areas where there are other multifamily properties which directly compete for residents.&#160; There is also limited competition from single family homes and condominiums for sale or rent.&#160; The competitive environment may have a detrimental effect on the Company&#146;s ability to lease apartments at existing and newly developed properties, as well as on rental rates.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, the Company competes with other real estate investors in seeking property for acquisition.&#160; These competitors include pension and investment funds, insurance companies, private investors, local owners and developers, and other apartment REITs.&#160; This competition could increase prices for properties that the Company would like to purchase and impact the Company&#146;s ability to achieve its long-term growth targets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company believes, however, that it is well-positioned to compete effectively for both residents and properties as a result of its:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">focus on service and resident satisfaction, as evidenced by both The Home Properties Pledge, which provides a money-back service guarantee and lease flexibility, and by its resident turnover ratio which is consistently below the industry average;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ability to issue UPREIT Units in purchase transactions, which provides sellers with the opportunity to defer taxes; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">unique repositioning strategy that differentiates the Company from its competitors.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">8<a name="PB_8_104549_141"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Market Environment</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The markets in which Home Properties operates could be characterized long term as stable, with moderate levels of job growth.&#160; After a recessionary period, starting in 2010 and expected to continue through 2015, many regions of the United States have been experiencing varying degrees of economic recovery resulting in improving job growth for both the country as a whole and the Company&#146;s markets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2013, job growth in the Company&#146;s markets was slightly behind the U.S. average with 1.2% job growth versus 1.6%, respectively.&#160; In 2014, job growth in the Company&#146;s markets continued to lag the U.S. average with a 1.2% growth rate versus 2.3%.&#160; However, the unemployment rate for the Company&#146;s markets of 5.1% continues to compare favorably to the country average of 5.4%.&#160; The Company&#146;s Boston, MA market experienced the lowest unemployment rate of 4.2%.&#160; This market represents 8.4% of the Company&#146;s total apartment unit count.&#160; Unemployment in the Company&#146;s largest market, Northern VA/DC with 26.6% of the Company&#146;s total apartment units, dropped from 4.6% at December 31, 2013 to 4.5% at December 31, 2014 and remains well below the country average.&#160; These two markets represent a combined 35% of the Company&#146;s total units with an unemployment rate below 5.0% as of December 31, 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">New construction in the Company&#146;s markets is low relative to the existing multifamily housing stock and compared to other regions of the country.&#160; In 2014, Home Properties&#146; markets represented 28.0% of the total estimated existing U.S. multifamily housing stock, but only 20.9% of the country&#146;s estimated new supply of multifamily housing&nbsp;units.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The information on the &#147;Market Demographics and Multifamily Supply and Demand&#148; tables on pages 10 and 11 were compiled by the Company from the sources indicated on the tables.&#160; The methods used include estimates and, while the Company feels that the estimates are reasonable, there can be no assurance that the estimates are accurate.&#160; There can also be no assurance that the historical information included on the tables will be consistent with future&nbsp;trends.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">An analysis of multifamily supply compared to multifamily demand can indicate whether a particular market is tightening, softening or in equilibrium.&#160; The fourth to last column in the &#147;Multifamily Supply and Demand&#148; table on page 11 reflects current estimated net new multifamily supply as a percentage of new multifamily demand for the Company&#146;s markets and the United States.&#160; For both the Company&#146;s markets and the country as a whole, net new supply is low compared to expected new demand.&#160; For the country, net new supply represents 64.1% of net new demand, creating an environment where both pricing and/or occupancy are expected to remain stable with room for some improvement.&#160; The relationship in the Company&#146;s markets is even better, where net new supply after obsolescence is expected to meet only 55.8% of the expected increasing demand for rental housing.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><i><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:9.0pt;font-style:italic;">(1)-(6)&nbsp;see footnotes on prior page</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">(7)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Estimated 2014 New Supply of Multifamily</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> =&#160; Multifamily permits (2014 figures U.S. Census Bureau, Mfg.&nbsp;&amp; Constr. Div., 5+ permits only) adjusted by the average % of permits resulting in a construction start (estimated at 95%).</font></p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">(8)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Estimated 2014 Multifamily Obsolescence</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> = Estimated 2014 Multifamily Housing Stock multiplied by the estimated % of obsolescence (0.5%).</font></p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">(9)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Estimated 2014 Net New Multifamily Supply</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> = Estimated 2014 New Supply of Multifamily - Estimated 2014 Multifamily Obsolescence.</font></p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">(10)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Estimated 2014 New Multifamily Household Demand</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> = 2014 job growth (Nonfarm, not seasonally adjusted payroll employment figures) (12/31/2013-12/31/2014) multiplied by the expected % of new household formations resulting from new jobs (66.7%) and the % of multifamily households in each market (based on Nielsen estimates).</font></p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">(11)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Expected Excess Demand</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> = Estimated 2014 New Multifamily Household Demand - Estimated 2014 Net New Multifamily Supply.</font></p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">(12)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Expected Excess Revenue Growth</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> = Expected Excess Demand divided by 2014 Multifamily Housing Stock.&#160; This percentage is expected to reflect the relative impact that changes in the supply and demand for multifamily housing units will have on occupancy rates and/or rental rates in each market, beyond the impact caused by broader economic factors, such as inflation and interest rates.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 1A.&#160; Risk Factors</font></u></b><a name="Item1a_RiskFactors_104709"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As used in this section, references to &#147;we&#148; or &#147;us&#148; or &#147;our&#148; refer to the Company, the Operating Partnership, and HPRS, taken as a whole.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our business is subject to uncertainties and risks.&#160; Please carefully consider the risk factors described below, which apply to Home Properties, the Operating Partnership, and HPRS, in addition to other risks set forth in this Form&nbsp;10-K.&#160; Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also impair our business or prospects.&#160; The risk factors we describe contain or refer to certain forward-looking statements.&#160; You should review the explanation of the limitations of forward-looking statements contained in the section entitled &#147;Forward-Looking Statements&#148; on page&nbsp;59 of this Form&nbsp;10-K.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Real Estate Investment Risks</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">We are subject to risks that are part of owning residential real estate.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Real property investments are subject to varying degrees of risk.&#160; If our communities do not generate revenues sufficient to meet operating expenses, debt service and capital expenditures, our cash flow and ability to make distributions to our stockholders will be adversely affected.&#160; A multifamily apartment community&#146;s revenues and value may be adversely affected by general economic conditions (including unemployment and erosion in the credit quality of the renter pool); local and regional economic conditions (including population shifts); local and regional real estate considerations (such as oversupply of or reduced demand for apartments); changes in home ownership or condominium affordability; the perception by prospective residents of the convenience and attractiveness of the communities or neighborhoods in which they are located and the quality of local schools and other amenities; and increased operating costs (including real estate taxes and utilities). Certain significant fixed expenses are generally not reduced when circumstances cause a reduction in income from a community.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">We depend on rental income for cash flow to pay expenses and make distributions.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are dependent on rental income from our multifamily properties to pay operating expenses, debt service and capital expenditures, and in order to generate cash to enable us to make distributions to our stockholders.&#160; If we are unable to attract and retain residents or if our residents are unable, due to an adverse change in the economic condition of the region or otherwise, to pay their rental obligations, our financial results and our ability to make expected distributions will be adversely affected.&#160; In addition, the weather and other factors outside of our control can result in an increase in the operating expenses for which we are responsible.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">An increase in operating expenses, including real estate taxes, would negatively affect our financial results.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Unanticipated increases in real estate taxes and other unanticipated or increased operating expenses cannot always be passed through to residents in the form of higher rents and may adversely affect financial results and our ability to make expected distributions.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Attractive acquisitions may not be available and acquisitions we may be able to make may fail to meet expectations.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We plan to continue to selectively acquire apartment communities that meet our investment criteria. &#160;We expect that other real estate investors, including insurance companies, pension funds, other REITs and other well-capitalized private investors will compete with us to acquire multifamily properties.&#160; This competition could increase prices for properties of the type we would likely pursue and adversely affect our growth, profitability and current strategy of targeting a similar range of acquisitions and dispositions.&#160; If we are able to make acquisitions, there are risks that those acquisitions will perform less favorably than we expect.&#160; Our estimates of future income, expenses and the costs of improvements or redevelopment that are necessary to allow us to operate an acquired property as originally intended may prove to be inaccurate.&#160; Other acquisition risks include environmental issues, tax reassessments, structural issues, competition, economic submarket changes and employment variables.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">13<a name="PB_13_103839_2897"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Real Estate Investment Risks (continued)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Real estate investments are relatively illiquid, and we may not be able to respond to changing conditions quickly.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Real estate investments are relatively illiquid and, therefore, we have limited ability to adjust our portfolio quickly in response to changes in economic or other conditions.&#160; In addition, the prohibition in the Internal Revenue Code (the &#147;Code&#148;) on REITs holding property for sale and related regulations may affect our ability to sell properties without adversely affecting distributions to stockholders.&#160; A number of our properties were acquired using UPREIT Units and four of those properties are still subject to certain agreements which may restrict our ability to sell such properties in transactions that would create current taxable income to the former owners.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Possible difficulties in selling apartment communities could limit our flexibility.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have identified certain of our communities that we intend to sell in 2015. We may encounter difficulty in finding buyers in a timely manner who are willing to pay acceptable prices for these communities. If we are unable to sell apartment communities or if we can only sell them at prices lower than are expected, then we may have to take on additional leverage in order to provide adequate capital to execute our strategies.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Competition could limit our ability to lease apartments or increase or maintain rents.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our apartment communities compete with other housing alternatives to attract residents, including other rental apartments, condominiums and single-family homes that are available for rent, as well as new and existing condominiums and single-family homes for sale.&#160; Competitive residential housing in a particular area could adversely affect our ability to lease apartment units and to increase or maintain rental rates.&#160; The recent challenges in the credit and housing markets have increased single-family housing inventory that may compete with our properties.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Repositioning and development risks could affect our profitability.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A key component of our strategy is to acquire properties and to reposition them for long-term growth.&#160; In addition, while we have made a decision to no longer include development of new properties as a strategy, we have one new development property that is in the process of being completed and another new development property that is substantially completed but has not achieved full lease up.&#160; Repositioning activities may require various governmental and other approvals, which have no assurance of being received.&#160; Our repositioning and limited remaining development activities generally entail certain risks, including the following:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">funds may be expended and management&#146;s time devoted to projects that may not be completed due to a variety of factors, including without limitation, the inability to obtain necessary zoning or other approvals;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">construction costs of a project may exceed original estimates, possibly making the economic return on a repositioned or developed property less than anticipated;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-17.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">occupancy rates and rents at a completed development project or at a repositioned property may be less than anticipated; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the operating expenses may be higher than anticipated.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If any of these risks materialized, the effect may negatively impact our financial results and reduce the funds available for distribution to our stockholders.&#160; Further, the repositioning and development of properties is also subject to the general risks associated with real estate investments.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Real Estate Investment Risks (continued)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Short-term leases expose us to the effects of declining market conditions.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Virtually all of the leases for our properties are short-term leases (generally, one year or less).&#160; Typically, our residents can leave after the end of a one-year lease term.&#160; As a result, our rental revenues are impacted by declines in market conditions more quickly than if our leases were for longer terms.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">A significant uninsured property or liability loss could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company carries commercial general liability, property and business interruption insurance with respect to our properties on terms we consider commercially reasonable.&nbsp; &nbsp; There are however certain types of extraordinary losses, such as losses for certain natural catastrophes and relating to environmental contamination, that are not insured, in full or part, because they are either uninsurable or the cost of insurance makes it, in management&#146;s view, economically impractical.&nbsp; If an uninsured loss occurred, we could incur significant expense.&nbsp; As a result of a catastrophic uninsured event impacting an entire property, we could lose our investment in and cash flow from, the affected property, and could be required to repay any indebtedness secured by that property and related taxes and other charges.&nbsp; If an uninsured liability to a third party were to occur, we would incur the cost of defense and/or settlement with or court ordered damages to, that third party.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Insurance costs and policy deductibles expose us to unpredictable expenses which may be material.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company&#146;s property insurance policies provide for a per occurrence deductible of $50,000 until exhaustion of $2.25 million annual aggregate self-insured retention, and then $100,000 per occurrence deductible.&nbsp; Earthquake, named windstorm, and flood losses are subject to higher deductibles but are not subject to the aggregate self-insured retention.&nbsp; Should a covered claim exceed these deductibles and self-insured retention, it would be 100% covered by insurance.&nbsp;&nbsp; The Company&#146;s general liability policies provide for a self-insured retention of $100,000 per occurrence and its workers&#146; compensation policies contains a $250,000 per claim deductible.&nbsp; These large deductible and self-insured retention amounts expose the Company to greater potential uninsured losses.&nbsp; Management believes that this exposure is justified by savings in insurance premium amounts and, in some cases, was necessary for the Company to secure coverage.&#160; However, the potential impact of poor claims experience could cause a significant increase in insurance premiums and deductibles or a decrease in the availability of coverage, either or which could expose the Company to even greater uninsured losses.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company also maintains a $50 million stand-alone terrorism policy with a $25,000 per occurrence deductible in regard to property damage and business interruption combined.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">The Company is subject to increased exposure to economic and other competitive factors due to concentration of its Properties in certain markets.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2014, approximately 26.6%, 24.9%, 14.0%, 8.5% and 8.5% (on an apartment unit basis) of the Company&#146;s Properties are located in the Washington, D.C., Baltimore, Philadelphia, Long Island and Northern New Jersey markets, respectively.&#160; The Company&#146;s current strategy is to reduce its concentration in the Washington,&nbsp;D.C. market to approximately 25%.&#160; If any one or more of such core markets is adversely affected by local or regional deteriorating economic conditions or other factors, the adverse impact on our results of operations could be greater than if our portfolio was more geographically diverse.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
