<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 7.</font></u></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</font></u></b><a name="Item7_ManagementsDiscussionAndAna_141934"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Overview</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations is intended to facilitate an understanding of the Company&#146;s business and results of operations.&#160; It should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements, the accompanying Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements and the selected financial data included in this Form&nbsp;10-K.&#160; This Form&nbsp;10-K, including the following discussion, contains forward-looking statements regarding future events or trends as described more fully under &#147;Forward-Looking Statements&#148; on page&nbsp;59.&#160; Actual results could differ materially from those projected in such statements as a result of the risk factors described in Item 1A, &#147;Risk Factors,&#148; of this Form&nbsp;10-K.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is engaged in the ownership, management, acquisition and repositioning of apartment communities in suburbs of major metropolitan areas, primarily along the East Coast of the United States.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company owned and operated 121 apartment communities with 42,107 apartments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Executive Summary</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company operated during 2014 in a stable economic environment, where the Company&#146;s markets and the country as a whole experienced job growth of 1.2% and 2.3%, respectively.&#160; This is consistent with the job growth in the Company&#146;s markets of 1.2% in 2013.&#160; An increase in job growth historically leads to household formations, which creates an increase in demand for rental housing.&#160; In addition, the credit crisis of the past recession has made it more difficult for apartment residents who may have considered purchasing a home to qualify for a mortgage.&#160; After years of home ownership being the number one reason our residents gave for moving out of our apartment communities, it dropped starting in 2007, such that it was the number five reason in 2013 and 2014.&#160; The combination of steady job growth and reduced flexibility for residents to purchase homes has created an environment supporting higher rental income growth and occupancy rates.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company owned 113 communities with 39,253 apartment units throughout 2013 and 2014 where comparable operating results are available for the years presented (the &#147;2014 Core Properties&#148;).&#160; Physical occupancies at the 2014 Core Properties remained constant at 95.2% between the years 2014 and 2013.&#160; Including bad debt in the calculation to arrive at &#147;economic occupancy&#148;, this metric also remained the same at 94.1%.&#160; The level of bad debt improved to 90 basis points in 2014 compared to 91 basis points in 2013.&#160; For 2015, we are projecting bad debt to be approximately 80 basis points of rental income plus utility recovery.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company uses a measurement referred to as Available to Rent, or &#147;ATR&#148;.&#160; This is a leading indicator of future occupancy rates and refers to units which will be available for rent, based upon leases signed or termination notices received relating to future move in/move out dates.&#160; As of the end of the first week of February, 2015 and 2014, our ATR was 5.1% and 7.1%, respectively.&#160; Average physical occupancy for the quarter ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 was at a level of occupancy at 95.0%, with a continuation of low resident turnover for 2014 of 39.9%, down from the 40.3% experienced in 2013.&#160; For 2015, we are projecting physical occupancy to be 20 basis points higher than 2014 based on current occupancy trends.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Total 2014 Core Properties rental revenue growth for 2014 was projected to be 3.2%, consisting of an increase of 3.0% in rental rate growth with economic occupancy to increase 0.2%.&nbsp; Actual results were positive 2.7% in rental rate growth with no change in economic occupancy resulting in 2.7% total rental revenue growth.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">36<a name="PB_36_111247_5796"></a></font></p>

<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Executive Summary (continued)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The guidance for 2015 Core Properties (apartment units owned throughout 2014 and 2015, the &#147;2015 Core Properties&#148;) total revenue growth is 3.0% at the midpoint of guidance.&nbsp; Rental rates are projected to increase 3.1%, including above-average rental increases at certain communities resulting from continued efforts to upgrade the properties.&#160; Economic occupancies are expected to increase 0.4% for the year, such that rental revenues are projected to increase 3.5%.&nbsp; The property other income growth rate is expected to be negative, decreasing total revenue growth by 0.5%, resulting in the net 3.0% total revenue growth projected. Property other income includes utility reimbursements which will be higher in years where we experience extreme winter weather conditions.&#160; For 2015, the Company has projected a normal winter resulting in lower utility reimbursements and corresponding utility expense.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">After four consecutive years of expense decreases (2009-2012), and a slight increase of 1.8% in 2013, the Company projected 2014 expenses to increase 3.5% at the midpoint of guidance.&#160; Actual results were an increase of 5.6% which included above average increases in repairs and maintenance costs, real estate taxes, property insurance and snow removal costs.&#160; For 2015, the Company expects savings in utilities, property insurance and snow removal costs to be partially offset by increases in repairs and maintenance costs, personnel costs (specifically from health care and the effects of new regulations) and real estate taxes.&#160; Expenses for 2015 Core Properties are projected to increase 1.5% at the midpoint of guidance.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">These revenue and expense projections result in 2015 Core Properties NOI growth of 4.0% at the midpoint of 2015 guidance.&#160; Markets where the Company expects NOI results above the average include: Boston 5.8%, Chicago 5.3%, Southeast Florida 5.1%, Philadelphia 4.7% and Northern New Jersey 4.2%.&#160; Markets with below average expectations include: Long Island 3.8%, Baltimore 3.6%, and Washington, D.C. 3.2%.&#160; Certain historical demographic information for these markets may be found in the tables on pages&nbsp;10 and 11 of this report.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the two items comprising NOI, revenue and operating expenses, the operating expense component is likely to be more volatile.&#160; It is difficult to predict the weather, which can have a significant effect, and there continues to be growing concern about real estate tax reassessments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has anticipated acquisitions in the range of $250 million to $350 million in its budget for 2015.&#160; The Company is committed to a disciplined approach to acquisitions.&#160; If cap rates stabilize, interest rates continue to be historically low, and NOI growth rates improve, the Company may take a more aggressive approach.&#160; The Company expects to dispose of between $100 million and $200 million of properties for 2015.&#160; After being a net seller in both 2013 and 2014, the Company is looking to become a net acquirer in 2015.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2015, the Company will target leverage at a level equal to or slightly less than the level at December&nbsp;31, 2014 of 38.0% of debt-to-total value (value as calculated under the terms of the line of credit facility) in order to meet the goals described above.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Results of Operations</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> (dollars in thousands, except unit and per unit data)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">C<i>omparison of year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 to year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013</i></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOI falls within the definition of &#147;non-GAAP financial measure&#148; set forth in Item 10(e)&nbsp;of Regulation S-K and, as a result, the Company is required to include in this report a statement disclosing the reasons why management believes that presentation of this measure provides useful information to investors.&#160; The Company believes that NOI is helpful to investors as a supplemental measure of the operating performance of a real estate company because it is a direct measure of the actual operating results of the Company&#146;s apartment communities.&#160; In addition, the apartment communities are valued and sold in the market by using a multiple of NOI.&#160; The Company also uses this measure to compare its performance to that of its peer group.&#160; For a reconciliation of NOI to income from continuing operations, please refer to Note 12 to Consolidated Financial Statements, under Part&nbsp;IV,&nbsp;Item 15 of this Form&nbsp;10-K.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2014, the Company acquired three apartment communities with a total of 1,052 units and placed into service another 404 units at two development communities (the &#147;2014 Acquisition Communities&#148;).&#160; In addition, the Company experienced full year results for the two apartment communities with 457 units acquired and one development community with 90 units placed into service during 2013 (the &#147;2013 Acquisition Communities&#148;).&#160; The Company has one community with 851 units undergoing significant renovations beginning in 2011 such that the operating results are not comparable to 2014 due to units being taken out of service during the redevelopment period (the &#147;Redevelopment Community&#148;).&#160; The inclusion of these acquired and developed communities generally accounted for the significant changes in operating results for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>

<td width="0%" valign="top" style="border:none;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:.5%;">
<p align="right" style="margin:.05in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>
<td width="8%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:8.0%;">
<p align="right" style="margin:.05in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>
<td width="7%" valign="top" style="border:none;border-bottom:double windowtext 2.25pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:7.0%;">
<p align="right" style="margin:.05in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$13,517</font></p>    </td>
<td width="0%" valign="top" style="border:none;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:.5%;">
<p align="right" style="margin:.05in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>
<td width="8%" valign="top" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:8.0%;">
<p align="right" style="margin:.05in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>
<td width="4%" valign="top" style="border:none;border-bottom:double windowtext 2.25pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:4.5%;">
<p align="right" style="margin:.05in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3.3%</font></p>    </td>
<td width="0%" valign="top" style="border:none;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:.5%;">
<p align="right" style="margin:.05in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2014, the Company disposed of three properties in four transactions with a total of 1,527 units, which had partial results for 2014 and full year results for 2013.&#160; During 2013, the Company disposed of four properties in four transactions with a total of 1,013 units, which had partial results for 2013.&#160; The results of these disposed properties have been reflected in discontinued operations and are not included in the tables above.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, income from continuing operations increased by $5,412 when compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to the following factors:&#160; an increase in rental income of $29,108, an increase in property other income of $3,820, a decrease in general and administrative expense of $1,821, and a decrease in interest expense of $10,441.&#160; These changes were partially offset by increases in operating and maintenance expense of $19,411, depreciation and amortization of $13,748, other expenses of $422, and impairment and other charges of $5,382.&#160; Each of the items are described in more detail below.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the $29,108 increase in rental income, $6,131 is attributable to the 2013 Acquisition Communities, $7,583 is attributable to the 2014 Acquisition Communities and $19 is attributable to the Redevelopment Community.&#160; The balance, an increase of $15,375, relates to a 2.7% increase from the 2014 Core Properties due primarily to an increase of 2.7% in weighted average rental rates to $1,329 from $1,294 per apartment unit, accompanied by consistent economic occupancy which was 94.1% for both periods.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the $1,841 increase in utility recovery revenue, $62 is attributable to the 2013 Acquisition Communities, $97 is attributable to the 2014 Acquisition Communities, and $1,719 relates to a 7.5% increase from the 2014 Core Properties, primarily due to a new trash recovery program that rolled out during 2013 and colder than normal temperatures in the winter of 2014 compared to warmer temperatures in the winter of 2013, leading to increased energy consumption and higher heat billed through to residents. These increases were partially offset by a $37 reduction for the Redevelopment Community.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The remaining property other income, which consists primarily of income from operation of laundry facilities, late charges, administrative fees, garage and carport rentals, revenue from corporate apartments, cable revenue, pet charges, and miscellaneous charges to residents, increased by $1,979.&#160; Of this increase, $249 is attributable to the 2013 Acquisition Communities, $389 is attributable to the 2014 Acquisition Communities, and $28 is attributable to the Redevelopment Community.&#160; The balance, an increase of $1,313, is attributable to the 2014 Core Properties resulting primarily from an increase of $610 due to higher late fees, damages and other charges and $462 relating to a higher level of incentive rebates.&#160; The remaining 2014 Core Properties increase of $241 primarily relates to increases in cable revenue, pet fee income and commercial rent, partially offset by lower corporate apartment revenue.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the $19,411 increase in operating and maintenance expenses, $2,501 is attributable to the 2013 Acquisition Communities, $4,350 is attributable to the 2014 Acquisition Communities and $54 is attributable to the Redevelopment Community.&#160; The balance, an increase of $12,506, relates to a 5.6% increase from the 2014 Core Properties primarily as a result of increases in repairs&nbsp;&amp; maintenance, personnel expense, property insurance, real estate taxes and snow removal costs.&#160; These increases were partially offset by decreases in legal&nbsp;&amp; professional and property management G&amp;A.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Natural gas heating costs were up $489, or 3.6%, from a year ago due to increased consumption resulting from a colder heating season in 2014 as compared to 2013 partially offset by lower commodity rates and a decreased dependence on fuel oil at a number of our properties where we converted to natural gas during 2014.&#160; For 2014, the Company&#146;s natural gas weighted average cost, including transportation of $3.00 per decatherm, was $7.62 per decatherm, compared to $7.78 per decatherm for the 2013 period, a 2.1% decrease.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January, 2015, the Company has fixed-price contracts covering 100% of its natural gas exposure for the balance of the 2014-15 heating season.&#160; Risk is further diversified by staggering contract term expirations.&#160; For the balance of the 2014-15 heating season, the Company estimates the average price per decatherm will be approximately $4.43, excluding transportation, which has historically approximated $3.00 per decatherm.&#160; For the 2015-16 heating season, the Company has fixed-priced contracts covering approximately 99.1% of its natural gas exposure for an estimated weighted average cost for fixed and floating rate contracts of $4.39 per decatherm, excluding transportation.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Water&nbsp;&amp; sewer costs were up $315, or 1.7%, from a year ago and are attributable to a new storm water tax experienced at several of our Maryland properties and general rate increases being assessed by local municipalities.&#160; The water&nbsp;&amp; sewer recovery program enabled the Company to recapture much of these rate increases from our residents.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Repairs&nbsp;&amp; maintenance expenses were up $1,577, or 5.0%, primarily due to proceeds from an insurance claim exceeding the cost basis of destroyed assets, related to a significant fire in the 2013 period of $1,227.&#160; Without the impact of the fire loss recovery, the recurring repairs&nbsp;&amp; maintenance expenses increased $350, or 1.1%.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Personnel expenses were up $1,366, or 2.6%, primarily due to an increase of $349, or 8.8%, in health insurance, which was driven by new fees assessed as part of the Affordable Care Act in 2014, coupled with the annual wage increase of 2.7%, or $1,050.&#160; These increases were partially offset by $70, or 9.1%, lower workers compensation insurance costs driven by favorable claims experience and $129, or 5.2%, lower incentive compensation for property management personnel.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Advertising expenses were up $6, or 0.1%, reflecting a continuing shift of $65 lower spending on print media and more emphasis on internet advertising and referral programs of $54 which contributed to a 3.3% increase in signed leases despite a 5.5% decrease in traffic in 2014 compared to 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Legal and professional costs were $598, or 34.2% lower, primarily due to fewer successful tax assessment challenges in 2014.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">40<a name="PB_40_112712_141"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Results of Operations (continued)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Office&nbsp;&amp; telephone expenses were up $257, or 4.0%, reflecting an increase in computer fees related to new internet-based application software which contributed to a 3.3% increase in signed leases in 2014 compared to 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property insurance costs increased by $3,037, or 48.1%, primarily due to higher self insured property losses in 2014 compared to 2013.&#160; The 2014 losses included $964 higher fire losses as compared to 2013, seventy-five properties experiencing $814 in losses due to pipe breaks caused by the extreme cold weather in all of our regions and $494 in water intrusion related losses due to heavy wind and severe rain storms that impacted a significant number of our properties in the Mid-Atlantic regions.&#160; The 2013 period contained a $288 one-time insurance reimbursement and experienced no significant storm or weather-related losses.&#160; The 2014 general liability losses were $189, or 11.3% higher than 2013, due to the impact of the harsher winter conditions experienced in 2014 compared to the mild winter of 2013.&#160; Without the impact of the major items above, recurring property and general liability insurance costs were up $288, or 8.9%.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Real estate taxes</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> were up $4,962, or 8.2%, primarily due to typical rate increases and annual tax assessment increases in our markets, some of which are triggered by our investments in apartment upgrades and repositioning.&#160; If not for successful tax assessment challenges and tax incentive programs which resulted in savings of $170 and $2,013 in 2014 and 2013, respectively, property taxes increased $3,120, or 5.0%. The Company continues to challenge tax assessments and apply for tax incentive programs on existing properties where appropriate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Snow removal costs were up $1,115, or 86.4%, primarily due to the Mid-Atlantic region experiencing significantly higher than normal snowfall and more numerous snow storms than in the 2013 period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property management general&nbsp;&amp; administrative costs decreased $335, or 2.0%.&#160; Despite increases in the number of apartment communities and units, the Company has been able to offset costs of growth due to its scalable operating platform, including efficiencies enabled by key application software investments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The operating expense ratio (the ratio of operating and maintenance expense compared to rental and property other income) for the 2014 Core Properties was 37.0% and 36.0% for 2014 and 2013, respectively.&#160; The 1.0% increase in 2014 is due in part to higher property insurance resulting from fire losses, lower level of tax refunds and the effects of a much harsher winter. In general, the Company&#146;s operating expense ratio is higher than that experienced by apartment owners in other parts of the country due to relatively high real estate taxes and heating costs in its markets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">General and administrative expenses (&#147;G&amp;A&#148;) decreased in 2014 by $1,821, or 6.4%, from $28,507 in 2013 to $26,686 in 2014.&#160; G&amp;A as a percentage of total revenues (including discontinued operations) was 3.9% for 2014 as compared to 4.2% for 2013. Stock-based compensation costs were $298, or 3.3% lower due primarily to $679 lower stock option expense due to the discontinuance of stock option grants in 2014 which was partially offset by $181 increase in executive equity compensation from the performance based restricted stock unit program that began in 2012 and $200 higher director restricted grants due to the addition of two new directors in 2014.&#160; In addition, the 2014 corporate bonus costs were $1,366, or 39.4%, less than the 2013 period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest expense decreased by $10,441, or 9.5%, in 2014 primarily as a result of paying off $79,000 in maturing loans on several Core Properties over the past year.&#160;&#160; In addition, only one of the three 2014 Acquisition Communities was acquired with assumed secured mortgage debt of $33,696 and both 2013 Acquisition Communities were acquired without secured mortgage debt.&#160; Refer to the information under the heading &#147;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#148; below for specific discussion of debt transactions impacting the average rate and overall interest expense.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">41<a name="PB_41_112939_7608"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Results of Operations (continued)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation and amortization expense increased $13,748, or 8.2%, due to a full year of depreciation expense for the 2013 Acquisition Communities, incremental depreciation on the capital expenditures for additions and improvements to the Core Properties of $122,379 and $128,357 in 2014 and 2013, respectively, as well as a partial year of depreciation expense for the 2014 Acquisition Communities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other expenses of $734 in 2014 and $312 in 2013 are property acquisition costs, primarily transfer taxes and title fees, which represent 0.52% and 0.56% of the total purchase price of the 2014 and 2013 Acquisition Communities, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Impairment and other charges of $5,382 were incurred in 2014 in connection with the decision to discontinue new property development.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net income decreased $2,108 in 2014 primarily due to $8,146 lower income from discontinued operations in 2014 compared to 2013.&#160; This is partially offset by an increase in income from continuing operations of $5,412 due to improved operating results from the 2014 Core Properties, the full year results of the 2013 Acquisition Communities plus a partial year impact of the operating results of the 2014 Acquisition Communities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Comparison of year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 to year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company owned 109 communities with 36,921 apartment units throughout 2012 and 2013 where comparable operating results are available for the years presented (the &#147;2013 Core Properties&#148;).&#160; For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, the 2013 Core Properties showed an increase in total revenues of 3.2% and a net operating income increase of 4.0% over the 2012 period.&#160; Property level operating expenses increased 1.8%.&#160; Average physical occupancy for the 2013 Core Properties was 95.2%, down from 95.5% in 2012, with average monthly rental rates of $1,295 per apartment unit, an increase of 3.2% over the 2012 period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A summary of the 2013 Core Properties NOI is as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2014, the Company disposed of three properties in three transactions with a total of 1,527 units, which had full year results for 2013 and 2012.&#160; During 2013, the Company disposed of four properties in four transactions with a total of 1,013 units, which had partial results for 2013 and full year results for 2012.&#160; The results of these disposed properties have been reflected in discontinued operations and are not included in the tables above.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, income from continuing operations increased by $32,885 when compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to the following factors:&#160; an increase in rental income of $32,553, an increase in property other income of $2,661, a decrease in general and administrative expense of $5,667, a decrease in interest expense of $9,795, and a decrease in other expenses of $2,429.&#160; These changes were partially offset by increases in operating and maintenance expense of $9,245, and depreciation and amortization of $11,843.&#160; Each of the items are described in more detail below.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the $32,553 increase in rental income, $14,606 is attributable to the 2012 Acquisition Communities, $99 is attributable to the 2013 Acquisition Communities, and $1,157 is attributable to the Redevelopment Community.&#160; The balance, an increase of $16,691, relates to a 3.2% increase from the 2013 Core Properties due primarily to an increase of 3.2% in weighted average rental rates to $1,295 from $1,254 per apartment unit, accompanied by consistent economic occupancy, which was 94.4% for both periods.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the $1,157 increase in utility recovery revenue, $558 is attributable to the 2012 Acquisition Communities, and $29 is attributable to the Redevelopment Community.&#160; The balance, an increase of $570, relates to a 2.7% increase from the 2013 Core Properties, primarily due to a new trash recovery program in 2013 and an increase in water&nbsp;&amp; sewer costs, which are billed to residents.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The remaining property other income, which consists primarily of income from operation of laundry facilities, late charges, administrative fees, garage and carport rentals, revenue from corporate apartments, cable revenue, pet charges, and miscellaneous charges to residents, increased by $1,504.&#160; Of this increase, $491 is attributable to the 2012 and 2013 Acquisition Communities and $1,128 is attributable to the 2013 Core Properties resulting primarily from an increase of $786 in damages and other charges due to increased resident turnover.&#160; The remaining Core Properties increase of $342 primarily relates to increases in renter&#146;s insurance door fees, pet fee income, corporate apartment revenue, late fees and incentive rebates, partially offset by lower cable revenue due to the 2012 period including nonrecurring income as a result of signing new contracts with cable providers which offer enhanced services in addition to basic cable.&#160; These increases were partially offset by a $115 reduction for the Redevelopment Community.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the $9,245 increase in operating and maintenance expenses, $5,092 is attributable to the 2012 Acquisition Communities, $159 is attributable to the 2013 Acquisition Communities and $114 is attributable to the Redevelopment Community.&#160; The balance, an increase of $3,867, relates to a 1.8% increase from the 2013 Core Properties primarily as a result of increases in personnel expense, real estate taxes and snow removal costs.&#160; These increases were partially offset by decreases in property insurance and property management G&amp;A.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Natural gas heating costs were up $87, or 0.7%, from 2012 due to increased consumption resulting from a colder heating season in 2013 as compared to 2012 partially offset by lower commodity rates.&#160; For 2013, the Company&#146;s natural gas weighted average cost, including transportation of $3.00 per decatherm, was $7.78 per decatherm, compared to $8.32 per decatherm for the 2012 period, a 6.5% decrease.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Water&nbsp;&amp; sewer costs were up $163, or 0.9%, from 2012 and are attributable to general rate increases being assessed by local municipalities.&#160; The water&nbsp;&amp; sewer recovery program enabled the Company to recapture much of these rate increases from our residents.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Repairs&nbsp;&amp; maintenance expenses were down $112, or 0.4%, primarily due to accounting for involuntary conversions related to fires and floods and the associated insurance claims at certain properties.&#160; Without the impact of these recoveries, the recurring repairs&nbsp;&amp; maintenance expenses increased $839, or 2.8%, as a result of higher resident turnover of 40.5% in 2013 as compared to 39.0% in 2012, which leads to higher spending on apartment turnover costs.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Personnel expenses were up $1,824, or 3.8%, primarily due to a significant increase of $1,830, or 95.2%, in health insurance, which was driven by higher self-insured claims in 2013, coupled with the annual wage increase of 2.6%, or $1,100.&#160; These increases were partially offset by $814, or 54.3%, lower workers compensation insurance costs driven by favorable claims experience and $377, or 14.1%, lower incentive compensation for property management personnel.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Results of Operations (continued)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Advertising expenses were down $48, or 1.0%, in 2013 reflecting the resident marketing program which placed less emphasis and spending on print media than in 2012 and more focus on internet-based methods and resident programs which contributed to a 2.5% increase in signed leases in 2013 compared to 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Office&nbsp;&amp; telephone expenses were down $187, or 3.0%, primarily due to $249 non-recurring refunds of certain resident fees from prior years in 2012.&#160; Without the impact of this non-recurring expense, office&nbsp;&amp; telephone expense decreased $62, or 1.0%.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property insurance costs decreased by $797, or 12.2%, primarily due to continued favorable close-outs of prior year self insured general liability claims, which yielded $1,378 in savings in 2013 compared to $338 in 2012 and favorable close-outs of prior year property claims of $505 in 2013.&#160; These savings were offset by property losses in 2013 of $2,644 compared to $1,421 in 2012, with the 2013 increase attributable to a significant fire at one of the Company&#146;s communities.&#160; Without the impact of the major items above, recurring property and general liability insurance costs were down $475, or 8.7%.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Real estate taxes</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> were up $2,448, or 4.5%, primarily due to typical rate increases and annual tax assessment increases in our markets, some of which are triggered by our investments in apartment upgrades and repositioning.&#160; If not for successful tax assessment challenges and tax incentive programs which resulted in savings of $2,098 and $1,306 in 2013 and 2012, respectively, property taxes increased $3,240, or 5.8%.&#160; The Company continues to challenge tax assessments on existing properties and apply for tax incentive programs for newly developed properties where appropriate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Snow removal costs were up $854, or 203.8%, primarily due to 2013 experiencing a more normal winter season compared to 2012 where most of our Northeast and Mid-Atlantic properties experienced the mildest winter on record.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property management general&nbsp;&amp; administrative costs decreased $324, or 2.0%.&#160; Despite increases in the number of apartment communities and units, the Company has been able to offset costs of growth due to its scalable operating platform, including efficiencies enabled by key application software investments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The operating expense ratio (the ratio of operating and maintenance expense compared to rental and property other income) for the 2013 Core Properties was 36.1% and 36.6% for 2013 and 2012, respectively.&#160; The 0.5% favorable improvement in 2013 is due in part to deliberate cost savings and safety initiatives implemented at the communities and rental income growth.&#160; In general, the Company&#146;s operating expense ratio is higher than that experienced by apartment owners in other parts of the country due to relatively high real estate taxes and heating costs in its markets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">General and administrative expenses (&#147;G&amp;A&#148;) decreased in 2013 by $5,667, or 16.6%, from $34,174 in 2012 to $28,507 in 2013.&#160; G&amp;A as a percentage of total revenues (including discontinued operations) was 4.2% for 2013 as compared to 5.2% for 2012.&#160; The 2012 costs included $1,580 in connection with the departure of an executive and represent acceleration of previously granted stock-based compensation as well as future payments for salary continuation.&#160; Employee stock-based compensation expenses were down $3,391, or 28.4%, in 2013, of which $3,910 was due to a final grant of arrears-based restricted stock and stock options in the 2012 period to executives, which did not occur in 2013 as the executive equity compensation switched primarily to a new three year performance restricted stock unit program in 2012.&#160; The cost of the performance based equity program was $519 higher in 2013 due to the impact of executives at, or near retirement age, being expensed immediately or over a one year shorter period in 2013.&#160; In addition, the 2013 corporate bonus costs were $922 less than the 2012 period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest expense decreased by $9,795, or 8.2%, in 2013 primarily as a result of paying off $250,000 in maturing loans on several Core Properties over the past year.&#160; In addition, both 2013 Acquisition Communities were acquired without secured mortgage debt and only one 2012 Acquisition Community was acquired with assumed secured mortgage debt of $7,284.&#160; Refer to the information under the heading &#147;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#148; below for specific discussion of debt transactions impacting the average rate and overall interest expense.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Results of Operations (continued)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Depreciation and amortization expense increased $11,843, or 7.6%, due to a full year of depreciation expense for the 2012 Acquisition Communities, incremental depreciation on the capital expenditures for additions and improvements to the Core Properties of $119,260 and $137,779 in 2013 and 2012, respectively, as well as a partial year of depreciation expense for the 2013 Acquisition Communities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other expenses of $312 in 2013 and $2,741 in 2012 are property acquisition costs, primarily transfer taxes and title fees, which represent 0.56% and 0.92% of the total purchase price of the 2013 and 2012 Acquisition Communities, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net income increased $27,957 in 2013 primarily due to an increase in income from continuing operations of $32,885 due to improved operating results from the 2013 Core Properties, the full year results of the 2012 Acquisition Communities plus a partial year impact of the operating results of the 2013 Acquisition Communities.&#160; This is partially offset by $5,601 lower income from discontinued operation in 2013 compared to 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">General</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s principal liquidity demands are expected to be distributions to the common stockholders and holders of UPREIT Units, capital improvements and repairs and maintenance for its properties, acquisition and debt repayments.&#160; The Company may also acquire equity ownership in other public or private companies that own and manage portfolios of apartment communities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company intends to meet its short-term liquidity requirements through cash flows provided by operating activities and its existing bank line of credit, described below.&#160; The Company considers its ability to generate cash to be adequate to meet all operating requirements, including availability to pay dividends to its stockholders and make distributions to its Unit holders in accordance with the provisions of the Internal Revenue Code, as amended, applicable to REITs.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To the extent that the Company does not satisfy its short-term liquidity requirements through net cash flows provided by operating activities and its existing bank line of credit, it intends to satisfy such requirements through proceeds from the issuance of unsecured senior notes and from the issuance of its common stock through its equity offering programs, described below, and from the sale of properties.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;3, 2014, Standard&nbsp;&amp; Poor&#146;s Ratings Services assigned a BBB issuer rating to the Company with a rating outlook of stable.&#160; On October&nbsp;6, 2014, Fitch,&nbsp;Inc. reaffirmed the Company&#146;s corporate credit rating&nbsp;of BBB with a rating outlook of positive. On December 5, 2014, Moody&#146;s Investors Service reaffirmed the Company&#146;s issuer rating of Baa2 with a stable outlook.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For 2015, plans include increasing the level of the value of unencumbered properties to approximately 58% of the portfolio and maintaining the debt-to-total market capitalization ratio at a level equal to the level at December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investing activities include the sale and purchase of properties and land for development, capital improvements to properties, redevelopment, construction in progress and predevelopment.&#160; The Company considers the sale of properties as a potential source of capital for funding acquisitions.&#160; Management&#146;s strategy also includes continuous repositioning and performance of selective rehabilitation in markets that are able to support rent increases, with a demand in the market for upgraded apartments.&#160; Changes between periods are primarily due to net acquisition and disposition activity, the rate of capital improvements and construction in progress expenditures for active development projects.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used in investing activities was $90 million during 2014.&#160; In 2014, the Company raised $211 million in net proceeds from the sale of three properties with 1,527 units.&#160; The Company purchased three properties with 1,052 units for $110 million.&#160; Cash outflows for capital improvements and redevelopment were $131 million and $8 million, respectively.&#160; Cash outflows for additions to construction in progress were $48 million which were primarily for the development of Eleven55 Ripley and The Courts at Spring Mill Station.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used in investing activities was $114 million during 2013.&#160; In 2013, the Company raised $188 million in net proceeds from the sale of four properties with 1,013 units.&#160; These proceeds were used to fund the purchase of two properties with 457 units for $56 million and the purchase of two land parcels for development for $42 million.&#160; Cash outflows for capital improvements and redevelopment were $137 million and $7 million, respectively.&#160; Cash outflows for additions to construction in progress were $62 million which were primarily for the development of Eleven55 Ripley and The Courts at Spring Mill Station.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Cash Flow Summary (continued)</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used in investing activities was $366 million during 2012.&#160; In 2012, the Company raised $150 million in net proceeds from the sale of six properties with 1,596 units.&#160; These proceeds were used to fund the purchase of three properties with 2,018 units for $290 million.&#160; Cash outflows for capital improvements and redevelopment were $153 million and $12 million, respectively.&#160; Cash outflows for additions to construction in progress were $62 million for development of The Apartments at Cobblestone Square, Eleven55 Ripley and The Courts at Spring Mill Station.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financing activities include proceeds from equity issuances, net debt proceeds or payments and dividend and distribution payments.&#160; Equity and debt activities are closely aligned with investing activities discussed above.&#160; The Company has elected to be taxed as a real estate investment trust (&#147;REIT&#148;) under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, which requires the Company to distribute annually at least 90% of its REIT taxable income to its shareholders.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used in financing activities totaled $210 million for 2014, primarily as a result of reducing secured indebtedness.&#160; Proceeds raised through the sale of common stock from stock option exercises of $22 million, combined with net proceeds from the unsecured line of credit of $76 million and proceeds from an unsecured loan of $100 million, were offset by scheduled payments on mortgages of $31 million, payoff of mortgages of $180 million and distributions paid to stockholders and UPREIT Unitholders of $197 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash used in financing activities totaled $192 million for 2013, primarily as a result of reducing secured indebtedness.&#160; Proceeds raised through the sale of common stock under the public offering of $268 million, the ATM offering of $29 million and from stock option exercises of $15 million, combined with net proceeds from the unsecured line of credit of $31 million were offset by scheduled payments on mortgages of $34 million, payoff of mortgages of $317 million and distributions paid to stockholders and UPREIT Unitholders of $182 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash provided by financing activities totaled $111 million for 2012.&#160; Net proceeds from the sale of common stock under the ATM offering were $145 million and $17 million from stock option exercises, for combined proceeds of $162 million.&#160; The Company raised an additional $210 million in combined net proceeds from the unsecured line of credit of $160 million and $50 million issued in unsecured notes.&#160; Total proceeds were partially offset by scheduled payments on mortgages of $36 million, payoff of mortgages of $67 million and distributions paid to stockholders and UPREIT Unitholders of $159 million.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Liquidity and Capital Resources (continued)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Unsecured Line of Credit</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2013, the Company had a $450 million unsecured line of credit agreement with M&amp;T Bank and U.S. Bank National Association, as joint lead banks, and nine other participating commercial banks, with an initial maturity date of August&nbsp;18, 2017 and a one-year extension, at the Company&#146;s option.&#160; The Company had $269 million outstanding under the credit facility on December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; The line of credit agreement provides the ability to issue up to $20 million in letters of credit.&#160; While the issuance of letters of credit does not increase the borrowings outstanding under the line of credit, it does reduce the amount available.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company had outstanding letters of credit of $3.8 million resulting in the amount available on the credit facility of $177.2 million.&#160; Borrowings under the line of credit bear interest at a variable rate based on LIBOR, plus a spread from 1.00% to 2.00% based on the Company&#146;s leverage ratio.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, based on the Company&#146;s leverage ratio, the LIBOR margin was 1.00%, and the one-month LIBOR was 0.19%; resulting in an effective rate of 1.19% for the Company.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Unsecured Term Loans</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;9, 2011, the Company entered into a $250 million five-year unsecured term loan with M&amp;T Bank as lead bank, and ten other participating lenders, which was set to mature on December&nbsp;8, 2016.&#160; The term loan generated net proceeds of $248 million, after fees and closing costs, which were used to pay off an unsecured term loan, purchase an unencumbered property and acquire land for future development.&#160; On August&nbsp;19, 2013, the Company amended the term loan agreement to extend the maturity date to August&nbsp;18, 2018.&#160; No other changes were made to the terms of the unsecured term loan.&#160; The loan bears monthly interest at a variable rate based on LIBOR, plus a spread from 1.00% to 2.00% based on the Company&#146;s leverage ratio.&#160; On July&nbsp;19, 2012, the Company entered into two interest rate swap agreements with major financial institutions that effectively convert the variable LIBOR portion of this loan to a fixed rate of 0.685% through December&nbsp;7, 2016.&#160; On November&nbsp;4, 2013, the Company entered into three additional interest rate swap agreements that effectively convert the variable LIBOR portion of this loan to a fixed rate of 2.604% for the period of December&nbsp;8, 2016 through August&nbsp;18, 2018.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, based on the Company&#146;s leverage ratio, the spread was 1.00%, and the swapped one-month LIBOR was 0.685%; resulting in an effective rate of 1.685% for the Company.&#160; The loan has covenants that align with the unsecured line of credit facility.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June&nbsp;28, 2013, the Company entered into an unsecured loan agreement with M&amp;T Bank with a September&nbsp;30,&nbsp;2013 maturity date.&#160; The note had a maximum principal amount of $75 million with monthly interest at a variable rate based on LIBOR, plus a spread from 1.00% to 2.00% based on the Company&#146;s leverage ratio.&#160; On June&nbsp;28, 2013, the Company borrowed $25 million which was repaid in its entirety on July&nbsp;12, 2013.&#160; Proceeds from this term loan were utilized to partially fund the repayment of secured debt.&#160; On August&nbsp;19, 2013, the loan commitment was terminated in connection with an amendment to the unsecured line of credit, as more fully described in Note 6 to Consolidated Financial Statements of this Form&nbsp;10-K.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;19, 2014, the Company entered into an unsecured loan agreement with M&amp;T Bank and borrowed $100 million with a May&nbsp;18,&nbsp;2015 maturity date.&#160; The note has a maximum principal amount of $100 million with monthly interest at a variable rate based on LIBOR, plus a spread from 1.00% to 2.00% based on the Company&#146;s leverage ratio.&#160; Proceeds from this term loan were utilized to pay down the line of credit.&#160; The loan has covenants that align with the unsecured line of credit facility.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Unsecured Demand Note</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June&nbsp;27, 2012, the Company entered into a loan agreement with M&amp;T Bank with a maximum principal amount of $100 million and monthly interest at a variable rate based on LIBOR, plus a spread from 1.00% to 2.00% based on the Company&#146;s leverage ratio.&#160; The Company borrowed the maximum amount of $100 million.&#160; Proceeds from this demand note were utilized to partially fund the purchase of a 1,350 unit apartment community on June&nbsp;28, 2012.&#160; During the fourth quarter, 2012, the Company repaid the $100 million note in full.</font></p>
